messages:
alice.sre: @channel Paging: p99 latency spike observed on streaming generate endpoints in us-west-2 — started ~14:03 UTC. Some requests are experiencing 5-10s tails and several streaming sessions stalled. Incident bot: ⚠️ Alert: streaming.tail_latency.p99 > 3s for 2m on service ‘redwood-gen-west’.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1134. Severity: P1. Paging on-call.

ben.infra: I'm on it. First look at node metrics — several GPU nodes showing long GC stalls and increased ECC correctable errors on host-group gpu-pool-11.

carla.runtime: Noted. Tracing shows KV cache misses spiking and a backlog in the streaming multiplexer. Backpressure is propagating to clients (chunked streams not flushed).

alice.sre: Customer impact check: internal SLOs show p95 still within target but p99 breached by ~2.2s. Dan, can you check support for customer-facing tickets so we can triage impact?

dan.support: Reached out to a customer on beta (org-id: brightwave). They report intermittent stalls and timeouts for long-running chat sessions. Logging shows reconnects at 14:05. I'll open incident notes in support queue.

eva.custsuccess: Heads up: two enterprise contracts in us-west-2, potential SLA triggers. Need ETA before we escalate externally.

ben.infra: Quick mitigation: I'm draining affected nodes from routing (adding them to maintenance set) and will force-fallback routing to GPU-quant-2 variants with spare capacity to reduce tail. Executing now.

carla.runtime: Suggest enabling short-term aggressive KV prefix caching for common prompts: config patch below. This should reduce cache misses while we stabilize nodes.

carla.runtime: ```json
{"kv_cache": {"prefix_cache_enabled": true, "ttl_ms": 60000, "max_entries": 200000}}
```

alice.sre: Ben, after drain, do we see request reroutes happening smoothly or are streaming sessions getting dropped?

ben.infra: Reroutes live. Most new requests go to fallback pool. Existing in-flight streaming sessions: some are resilient, some stalled — likely because the worker paused due to thermal throttle. I'm kicking a rolling restart on 3 of the worst nodes to clear the stuck streams.

incident-bot: Note: automatic fallback policy applied: model-variant fallback to cpu-quant-2 for non-low-latency tiers.

carla.runtime: Observed ECC correctable error rate on GPU 3/8 on node gpu-11-07 increasing rapidly correlated with the stalls. Thermal sensors also trending up (GPU package temp hitting 88C). Looks like hardware-level throttling kicks intermittently.

ben.infra: Confirmed. I'm marking gpu-11-07 as flaky and removing it from pool. Scheduling immediate hardware quarantine.

alice.sre: Live mitigation summary: 1) Drain and fallback routing — done. 2) Rolling restart of hot workers — in progress. 3) Aggressive KV caching toggle — applied. 4) Hardware quarantine on affected nodes — initiated. Any impact to throughput?

carla.runtime: Throughput dropped ~12% while rerouting but latency p99 improving from 5.1s to 2.4s after fallbacks. Streaming stall count dropped ~70% after restarts.

dan.support: Logged outreach to impacted customers and queued SOC message. Customers want timeline — ETA for full remediation?

ben.infra: Hardware replacement ETA for quarantined nodes ~3 hours (spare parts in us-west-2). We'll keep fallback routing for steady state until nodes are replaced.

eva.custsuccess: I'll prep a short customer-facing blurb: acknowledgement, mitigation steps, and that we're monitoring. Share before you send.

alice.sre: Action items: ben => finalize quarantine + HW ticket (TICKET-4891), carla => validate cache regressions against eval set, dan/eva => customer comms, I'll run post-mortem timeline capture.

carla.runtime: Also collecting model-level traces for the experience: evidence suggests the stalls were exacerbated by long-history KV thrashing for larger context requests. Will prepare an eval comparing latency with and without prefix caching.

ben.infra: Ticket filed: HW-4891, spare node replacement scheduled. Nodes removed: gpu-11-07, gpu-11-09 (both with elevated ECC correctables).

incident-bot: Update: Incident INC-2026-1134 status -> mitigated. Monitoring for regressions.

alice.sre: TL;DR for handoff: immediate customer-facing impact reduced, p99 back under ~2.5s after fallbacks, hardware faults (ECC + thermal) on two GPUs caused throttling and streaming stalls. On-call handoff to infra @ 17:00 UTC for hardware replacement follow-up and to SRE @ 18:00 UTC for post-incident analysis.

ben.infra: Leaving handoff notes in the ticket: what I did, commands, nodes quarantined, alt routing details.

carla.runtime: I'll drop the eval artifact and the diff of traces into the incident ticket. Also recommend we add an automated thermal->fallback policy: when GPU package temp > 85C and ECC correctables spike, proactively migrate streaming sessions off that node.

alice.sre: +1 on the policy. For now, we'll keep this incident open for follow-ups but marking live mitigation complete. Great work team. :thumbsup:

dan.support: Closing customer alerts for now; will reopen if customers report new issues.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1134 will be transitioned to 'postmortem' channel at 2026-05-14T19:00:00Z.
